latest.question: Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance in light of Drogheda Rural’s success in delivering the highest number of new-build homes per capita and already achieving his 83,000 housing target per person, with the Housing Infrastructure Services Company (HISCo) a key contributor, to provide, in tabular form, details of planned HISCo investment, including ISIF-supported investment, for each year from 2026 to 2030, broken down by local authority and, where available, by rural areas and villages, towns and cities; and to identify the number of homes each investment is expected to facilitate.
latest.reply:
In response to the Deputy's question I am informed as follows.
The Ireland Strategic Investment Fund (ISIF) invests on a commercial basis to support economic activity and employment in Ireland. As part of its housing investment strategy, ISIF invests across the capital structure to support the delivery of new homes across a range of dwelling type and tenure, including through the provision of development finance, equity capital and investment in enabling infrastructure. To date, ISIF has committed over €2.5 billion to housing-related investments.
ISIF has committed €61.5 million to HISCo, a 50:50 joint venture with Cork County Council to provide infrastructure to enable residential development, as part of its broader housing investment programme. ISIF does not disclose details of potential investments which have not been completed, as such information may be commercially sensitive. Accordingly, ISIF is not in a position to provide projected investment in HISCo for each year from 2026 to 2030.
ISIF's housing investments are made on a commercial basis and are assessed on their individual merits and their potential to support increased housing delivery. ISIF will continue to consider investment opportunities which are consistent with its statutory mandate and investment strategy and are complementary to other State initiatives in the housing sector.

latest.question: Deputy Catherine Callaghan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance if he will urgently review the exclusion of HGV driving schools from the diesel rebate scheme in view of the substantial fuel costs incurred by these businesses, the essential service they provide in training HGV and bus drivers, and the potential impact on driver supply to the transport industry.
latest.reply:
The Diesel Rebate Scheme (DRS) is a State aid that operates under Article 7(2) of Council Directive 2003/96/EC (Energy Tax Directive/ETD).
Article 7(2) explicitly allows EU Member States to apply a differentiated rate of excise duty to gas oil (auto diesel) used for commercial purposes, provided that the EU minimum levels of taxation are respected.
The ETD limits the scope of "commercial gas oil" to auto diesel used by specific segments of road transport. In line with this, the scope of Ireland’s DRS is defined by reference to road transport licensing criteria and includes licensed road haulage (goods transport) and passenger transport operators (such as bus and coach services).

latest.question: Deputy Ken O'Flynn asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether he is aware that some homeowners and tenants in areas classed as at risk of flooding report being unable to obtain any home or contents insurance, including cover for fire and theft, and not only flood cover; and whether his department or the Central Bank holds data on the number of such refusals.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 404 and 405 together.
The Government is taking a comprehensive and proactive approach to improving the affordability and availability of flood insurance in the Irish insurance market with the implementation of refoms under the Action Plan for Insurance Reform 2025-2029.
The decision on whether to offer home insurance, level of premiums charged, and the policy terms applied are matters for individual insurers based on an actuarial assessment of the risks they are willing to accept. The Solvency II Directive restricts Member States in terms of intervening in insurers’ pricing or underwriting decisions. Insurers rely on their own claims’ histories, risk assessments, and cost projections when deciding whether to provide cover. Factors such as inflation in building materials and labour are also influencing premium levels across the sector.
In terms of flood insurance, the Central Bank of Ireland has undertaken extensive research into the nature and scale of the flood insurance protection gap in Ireland. They found that 1 in 20 buildings (approximately 5%) have limited access to flood insurance; and that 54% of this gap is concentrated in Dublin, Cork, Louth, Clare, and Kildare. Neither my Department nor the Central Bank of Ireland hold data on the refusal of home insurance or flood insurance.

latest.question: Deputy Ken O'Flynn asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether an insurer is required to tell a customer the basis on which their property has been classified as at risk of flooding; whether any process exists for a homeowner with no recorded flood history to have that classification reviewed; and, if not, whether he will consider requiring one.
latest.reply:
The Government remains committed to protecting Ireland’s present and future generations by investing in climate adaptation measures to manage the impacts of extreme weather. Accordingly, €1.3 billion has been committed to the delivery of flood relief schemes over the lifetime of the National Development Plan (NDP) to 2030. This will protect approximately 23,000 properties across various communities from river and coastal flood risk.
In terms of flood insurance, the Central Bank of Ireland has undertaken extensive research into the nature and scale of the flood insurance protection gap in Ireland. They found that 1 in 20 buildings (approximately 5%) have limited access to flood insurance; and that 54% of this gap is concentrated in Dublin, Cork, Louth, Clare, and Kildare.
In terms of assessing flood risk, insurers use a variety of different flood data models (both internally developed models and flood models procured from third party vendors). Insurers will generally utilise (i) flood risk maps licenced from a third-party consultancy; (ii) bespoke flood maps based on individual historical claims experience/risk surveys undertaken of locations, and (iii) other information such as the flood defence benefit area data provided to Insurance Ireland by the OPW under the terms of the MOU, if applicable.
Insurance undertakings are bound by the provisions of the Central Bank’s Consumer Protection Code (the Code) in their dealings with consumers for the provision of financial services.

latest.question: Deputy Ann Graves asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether he acknowledges that further price increases on e-liquid products in budget 2027 could result in consumers switching to cheaper illicit vaping products or returning to smoking.
latest.reply:
The E-liquid products tax was legislated for in Finance Act 2024, and it came into effect on 1 November 2025. The tax applies to both nicotine-containing and non-nicotine containing e-liquid products.
The primary purpose of EPT is to address public health concerns and to account for the negative externalities created by the consumption of such products. We are still learning about the long-term risks of vaping, over time these risks may cause diseases such as heart disease, lung disease and cancer. Ireland is committed to protecting our children and young people from the harms caused by nicotine use. Ireland’s specific tax per millilitre is in line with the taxation approach adopted in several other EU Member States.
As with all taxes, Revenue's approach to EPT is to support compliant businesses and taxpayers, while using intelligence-led interventions and enforcement measures to detect, disrupt and pursue illicit activity in the vaping market. Revenue is undertaking the appropriate compliance work to ensure that businesses are properly registered for supply of e-liquid products. EPT is collected on a self-assessment basis and compliance with the law is enforced using the full range of compliance interventions and enforcement provisions for self-assessed taxes. Revenue compliance interventions are undertaken on a risk-assessed basis and EPT may be examined as part of cross tax head checks.

latest.question: Deputy Pádraig O'Sullivan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether his Department has assessed Poland's decision to apply an 8% VAT rate to petrol and diesel from 3 October 2026; whether such a measure is compatible with the EU VAT Directive; whether he has sought greater flexibility on fuel VAT at EU level; and the estimated cost to the Exchequer of each one percentage point reduction in VAT on petrol and diesel.
latest.reply:
The EU VAT Directive which Irish VAT law is obliged to comply, generally holds that all goods and service are liable for VAT at the standard rate which Member States must set at a minimum of 15%. Ireland currently charges a standard rate of 23%.
If a good or service is included in a list of goods and services under Annex III of the Directive, a reduced rate of VAT or exemption may be applied. Member States are permitted to apply up to two reduced rates at a minimum of 5%. Ireland currently has two reduced rates of VAT of 13.5% and 9%. Member States may also avail of a derogation under the terms of the Directive that allows for a reduced rate of VAT be applied to specific goods and services that have historically been charged below the standard rate and not included under Annex III. Reduced rates applied because of a derogation cannot be moved lower than 12%.
As auto fuels are not included under Annex III there is no legal basis to apply a VAT rate below 15%. As such the standard rate of VAT, currently 23%, applies to auto fuels. This rate can be reduced as low as 15% but would require all goods and services at 23% to be moved to 15%. The estimated cost of a 1% reduction in the standard rate of VAT is €707m. The full year cost of the standard rate of VAT being reduced from 23% to 15% is estimated to be €5.7 billion.
It should be noted that any VAT reduction may not be passed to consumers.

latest.question: Deputy Ken O'Flynn asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance if his Department has assessed the extent to which the limitation of help-to-buy relief to income tax and DIRT paid in the State in the four years preceding the year of application reduces or removes eligibility for former residents who have recently returned to the State after a period of employment abroad; whether any data is held on the number of help-to-buy claimants who were not tax resident in the State for part of that four year period; whether any alternative support for such returning former residents has been considered.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 395 and 396 together.
The Help to Buy (HTB) incentive, is a tax-based scheme to assist first-time purchasers with the deposit they need to buy or build a new house or apartment. It also aims to encourage additional supply of new houses by supporting demand.
Based on the latest available data (30 September 2026), the scheme has supported over 70,000 individuals or couples to buy or build their own home.
HTB provides a refund of Income Tax and Deposit Interest Retention Tax (DIRT) paid in Ireland over the previous four years, subject to limits outlined in the legislation.
The level of support available to first time buyers under the HTB scheme, is whichever is the lesser of:
• €35,000 (from 07 October 2026); or
• 10 per cent of the purchase price of the new property; or
• the amount of Income Tax and DIRT paid in the four years before application for the relief.
For a property to qualify for the HTB scheme, it must be new or converted for use as a dwelling, having not previously been used as a dwelling. Additionally, the purchase value/approved valuation of the property must not exceed €500,000.
It is a principle of taxation that those who benefit from an Income Tax or a DIRT refund must have paid the Income Tax or DIRT in the first place. examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.
The project received approval from my Department to commence construction in January 2026. More recently, Department officials were notified by the school authorities that construction has now commenced. Expected completion to coincide with the start of the new school year.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
